Create garagecreate-garage

Make a garage available with the capacity chosen by the user.

Actor: Garage user. · required

Flow

  1. The user requests a new garage from the console menu.
  2. The user enters its capacity.
  3. The system validates the capacity and creates an empty garage with that limit.
  4. The system confirms that the garage is ready to use.

Alternatives

  • Invalid capacity: explain the problem and allow correction without crashing or creating an invalid garage.
  • Initial vehicles: the application must also support creating a garage populated from the start. Initial vehicles must satisfy the same validity, uniqueness and capacity rules as vehicles parked later. The assignment does not specify how those initial vehicles are supplied.

Done when

  • A valid request creates a garage with the chosen capacity.
  • Its vehicle collection is stored privately using a list.
  • It can start empty or with valid initial vehicles without exceeding capacity.
  • Invalid input is handled with clear feedback.

Optional extensions are listed separately: multiple garages, configuration, file loading and sized spaces. Names, dimensions and JSON files are not required inputs to this basic flow.

Find vehicle by registrationfind-vehicle

Find a specific parked vehicle using its registration number.

Actor: Garage user. · required

Flow

  1. The user requests registration lookup from the console menu.
  2. The user enters a registration number.
  3. The system searches the parked vehicles without distinguishing uppercase and lowercase letters.
  4. The system displays the matching vehicle and its properties.

Alternatives

  • No match: explain that no vehicle with that registration is parked.
  • Invalid input: explain the problem and allow correction without crashing.

Done when

  • ABC123, Abc123 and AbC123 find the same vehicle.
  • The result identifies the matching parked vehicle, or clearly reports no match.
  • Searching leaves the garage unchanged.

List parked vehicleslist-vehicles

See which vehicles are currently parked and their properties.

Actor: Garage user. · required

Flow

  1. The user requests the list of parked vehicles from the console menu.
  2. The system retrieves the vehicles currently in the garage.
  3. The system displays each vehicle's registration, type and vehicle properties.

Alternatives

  • Empty garage: explain that no vehicles are parked.

Done when

  • Every parked vehicle is included once.
  • The user can distinguish vehicles and inspect their properties.
  • Vehicles outside the garage are not included.
  • Listing leaves the garage unchanged.

List vehicle types and countslist-vehicle-types

See how many vehicles of each type are parked in the garage.

Actor: Garage user. · required

Flow

  1. The user requests a summary by vehicle type from the console menu.
  2. The system groups the parked vehicles by type and counts each group.
  3. The system displays the vehicle types present and their counts.

Alternatives

  • Empty garage: explain that no vehicles are parked.

Done when

  • Each displayed count reflects the vehicles currently parked of that type.
  • The counts add up to the number of parked vehicles.
  • Vehicles outside the garage are not counted.
  • Viewing the summary leaves the garage unchanged.

Requirements: GAR-02 GAR-08 GAR-11 GAR-12

Navigate garage menusnavigate-menus

Reach the required garage functions through the console interface.

Actor: Garage user. · required

Flow

  1. The system presents the main menu and its available choices.
  2. The user selects a function or submenu.
  3. The system opens the requested interaction and shows the available choices.
  4. The user can continue with a function or return to the main menu.

Alternatives

  • Invalid choice: explain the available choices and allow another selection without crashing.
  • A garage is needed: explain that a garage must first be created before the requested operation can continue.

Done when

  • All required functions are reachable through text-based main and submenus.
  • Garage creation with user-specified capacity and application exit are reachable.
  • Invalid navigation does not crash the application or change garage contents.

Screen layouts, keyboard shortcuts and a rich dashboard are separate implementation choices or optional enhancements.

Requirements: GAR-11 GAR-12 GAR-13

Park vehiclepark-vehicle

Put a vehicle in the garage when there is capacity available.

Actor: Garage user. · required

Flow

  1. The user requests parking from the console menu and supplies or selects a vehicle.
  2. The system checks the vehicle details, registration uniqueness and available capacity.
  3. The system adds the vehicle to the garage.
  4. The system confirms that the vehicle is parked.

Alternatives

  • Invalid details: explain the problem and allow correction without crashing.
  • Duplicate registration: reject the request and preserve the vehicles already parked.
  • Garage full: explain that no capacity is available and leave the garage unchanged.

Done when

  • A valid vehicle is added when capacity is available.
  • Parking does not exceed the chosen garage capacity or introduce a duplicate registration.
  • A rejected request leaves the existing vehicles unchanged.
  • The user receives a clear success or failure message.

Optional extensions are listed separately: space selection, dimensions and filtering eligible vehicles. A separate catalogue and numbered parking-space objects are not required for basic parking.

Quit applicationquit-application

End the running garage application through its interface.

Actor: Garage user. · required

Flow

  1. The user chooses the exit option from the console menu.
  2. The system ends the menu interaction and shuts down normally.

Alternatives

  • Invalid menu choice: keep the application running, explain the available choices and allow another selection.

Done when

  • The user can end the application without forcibly closing the console.
  • Choosing exit terminates the running application normally.

Saving garage state between runs is an optional enhancement; this use case does not require persistence or a confirmation prompt.

Remove vehicleremove-vehicle

Take a parked vehicle out of the garage and make its capacity available again.

Actor: Garage user. · required

Flow

  1. The user requests vehicle removal from the console menu.
  2. The user identifies the parked vehicle.
  3. The system finds the vehicle and removes it from the garage.
  4. The system confirms that the vehicle has been removed.

Alternatives

  • Vehicle not found: explain that no matching vehicle is parked and leave the garage unchanged.
  • Invalid input: explain the problem and allow correction without crashing.

Done when

  • The identified vehicle is no longer parked in the garage.
  • Its capacity is available for another vehicle.
  • Other parked vehicles remain unchanged.
  • Registration lookup ignores letter case, and success or failure is clearly reported.

Requirements: GAR-07 GAR-09 GAR-11 GAR-12 GAR-13

Search parked vehiclessearch-vehicles

Find parked vehicles matching one or several chosen properties.

Actor: Garage user. · required

Flow

  1. The user requests vehicle search from the console menu.
  2. The user supplies one or more criteria using shared vehicle properties and, when wanted, vehicle type.
  3. The system finds parked vehicles that match all supplied criteria.
  4. The system displays the matching vehicles and their properties.

Alternatives

  • One criterion: search using just that criterion, such as colour.
  • Combined criteria: apply the criteria together, such as black vehicles with four wheels, or pink motorcycles with three wheels.
  • No matches: clearly report that no parked vehicles match.
  • Invalid values: explain the problem and allow correction without crashing.

Done when

  • Each shared vehicle property can be used for searching, alone or in combination with the others.
  • Type filtering can be combined with shared-property criteria.
  • Every result matches all supplied criteria, and the garage remains unchanged.

Searching properties specific to a subclass is an optional enhancement.

Create garage with sized spacescreate-garage-with-dimensions

Create a garage whose spaces have individual length, width and height limits.

Actor: Garage user. · optional

Flow

  1. The user supplies the garage name and the dimensions of its parking spaces.
  2. The system validates the name and space dimensions.
  3. The system registers the garage with the supplied spaces and confirms success.

Alternatives

  • Invalid dimensions: explain the problem and leave the garage collection unchanged.
  • Duplicate name: reject creation and preserve the existing garage.

Done when

  • Every created space retains its configured dimensions.
  • A rejected request does not add a partial garage.
  • Sized spaces remain an optional extension of the basic capacity-based garage.

Requirements: OPT-08

Create or import catalogue vehiclecreate-vehicle

Add a valid vehicle to the shared catalogue before parking it, with optional immediate parking.

Actor: Garage user. · optional

Flow

  1. The user enters vehicle details or selects a vehicle JSON file.
  2. The system validates the vehicle and checks registration uniqueness.
  3. If the user selected a garage, the system attempts to park the vehicle there.
  4. The system adds the vehicle to the catalogue and confirms success.

Alternatives

  • Invalid details or file: explain the problem and leave the catalogue unchanged.
  • Duplicate registration: reject the vehicle and preserve the existing catalogue.
  • Parking rejected: explain the failure and do not register the new vehicle in the catalogue.

Done when

  • Successful creation adds exactly one valid vehicle with a unique registration.
  • A vehicle may remain unparked in the catalogue.
  • Immediate parking must succeed before catalogue registration is committed.
